cards.headline: Pusha T stole the beat for his Drake diss
cards.snippet: In 2018, during his feud with Drake, Pusha-T released "The Story of Adidon," a diss track rapped over the beat from Jay-Z's "The Story of O.J." He premiered it on Hot 97, then posted it on Soundcloud. The song alleges Drake fathered a son with a porn star and kept the child secret. It also took aim at Drake's parents and at his collaborator Noah "40" Shebib. The cover image showed Drake in blackface, which Pusha-T insisted was a real photo and not artwork.
cards.context: Part of the Pusha-T and Drake feud, 2018.

cards.headline: A lyric about credit drew an ADL response
cards.snippet: In July 2017, soon after Jay-Z released 4:44, a line in "The Story of O.J." about Jewish people owning property in America set off debate on social media. The Anti-Defamation League said it didn't think Jay-Z meant to promote anti-Semitism. It still said the lyric played into stereotypes about Jews and money. Manager Guy Oseary, who is Jewish, and Russell Simmons defended it. Oseary called it a compliment, an example of wise financial choices.
cards.context: Reaction came days after the 4:44 release in July 2017.

cards.headline: A plea to stop dying over turf that was never yours
cards.snippet: Street gangs fight over territory that is ultimately government owned. Jay-Z, who knew how violent dealing could be, retired from the street life and urges other dealers to do the same, including by owning property.
cards.context: Top comment (13,000 likes) quotes the rented-neighborhood twist. Another says he explained how to clean dirty money while stopping gentrification.
